description: Budget management platform for service businesses. This file is the durable feature queue for the multi-agent harness.

features.name: harness_bootstrap
features.title: Bootstrap multi-agent harness
features.description: Add the repository harness inspired by betta-tech/ejemplo-harness-subagentes and adapt it to Bambu System.
acceptance: AGENTS.md acts as the progressive-disclosure map for agents
feature_list.json tracks one feature at a time with valid statuses
progress/current.md and progress/history.md persist session state
docs/architecture.md, docs/conventions.md, and docs/verification.md define project-specific standards
CHECKPOINTS.md gives reviewers objective final-state criteria
.codex/agents contains leader, implementer, and reviewer roles
init.ps1/init.sh run harness validation plus repository checks

features.name: codex_subagents
features.title: Replace Claude harness entrypoint with Codex subagents
features.description: Remove CLAUDE.md and make Codex subagent profiles the required orchestration roles.
acceptance: CLAUDE.md is removed because Codex reads AGENTS.md directly
.codex/agents contains leader, implementer, and reviewer profiles
Harness validation requires .codex/agents instead of Claude-specific files
No repository harness files reference Claude-specific entrypoints

features.name: budget_authorization_contracts
features.title: Harden budget ownership and category authorization
features.description: Refactor budgets and budget categories so reads and mutations enforce authenticated ownership or admin contracts before later UI work.
acceptance: getBudgets, getBudgetBySlug, getBudgetById, duplicate, update, and delete only expose or mutate budgets owned by the authenticated user
Budget mutations call auth() first, validate input with schemas, verify ownership before writing, and return consistent { error } results
BudgetCategory actions are explicitly admin-only through requireAdminSession() or converted to a documented user-owned model
Budget create/update/delete flows have no debug console.log statements
Manual smoke covers budget list, detail, create, edit, duplicate, delete, and budget categories

features.name: settings_server_action_auth
features.title: Secure settings server actions
features.description: Make settings mutations derive identity from the authenticated session instead of trusting client-sent user ids.
acceptance: updateName, updateEmail, updatePassword, enable2FA, disable2FA, and updateProfileImage call auth() and do not trust a client-provided user id
Account, email, password, 2FA, and profile image inputs validate through schemas/settings.ts
Settings actions are split by account and security responsibility with read helpers kept separate from mutations
The settings page keeps a server-side shell where viable and scopes client components to forms, dialogs, or interactive controls
Manual smoke covers account updates, email or password changes, profile image updates, and 2FA enable or disable flows

features.name: runtime_lazy_sdk_initialization
features.title: Lazy initialize runtime SDK clients
features.description: Move OpenAI, Resend, Cloudinary, and runtime URL configuration out of module scope so Next.js build and runtime contexts load safely.
acceptance: OpenAI, Resend, and Cloudinary clients are created through lazy getters or one-time configuration helpers
Environment variables and base URLs are read close to use and fail with clear errors when required values are missing
The AI chat streaming route imports domain helpers and keeps route-handler logic focused on request parsing, auth, and streaming response
No runtime SDK performs network-client initialization solely because a module was imported
Verification includes init.ps1 and pnpm build when the environment permits, plus focused smoke for affected AI, email, or upload paths

features.name: platform_dependency_patch_review
features.title: Review and patch Next and React dependencies
features.description: Run a controlled platform upgrade for Next.js, React, and React DOM to patched compatible versions.
acceptance: Next.js, React, and React DOM target versions are checked against the current patched release line before editing package files
package.json and the lockfile are updated together with no unrelated dependency churn
Any migration notes or breaking changes are documented in progress/current.md or a feature report
Verification includes init.ps1 and pnpm build when environment variables permit
Manual smoke covers auth, dashboard navigation, and AI chat after the upgrade

features.name: ai_chat_modularization
features.title: Split AI chat UI, streaming, history, and upload responsibilities
features.description: Reduce the AI chat monolith by moving chat state, history, image upload, rendering, and server message construction into focused modules.
acceptance: AIChat.tsx is reduced to a small shell or orchestrator under the repository file-size guidance
Session state, history, and image upload live in focused hooks that can be reasoned about independently
Message list, input, history panel, and chat actions are separate components with clear props
OpenAI client access and chat message construction live in server/domain helpers while the stream route stays thin
BudgetContext coupling is isolated behind an adapter instead of being buried throughout reusable UI
Manual smoke covers streaming, abort or error handling, image upload, save history, rename, and delete

features.name: budget_form_and_cache_refactor
features.title: Refactor budget forms, filters, preview, and query cache
features.description: Split the budget create/edit flow into focused sections and centralize filter parsing, query keys, invalidation, and domain helpers.
acceptance: Budget query keys and invalidation helpers are centralized for budgets and budget categories
Budget list filter parsing and URL/query-state handling live in focused filter helpers or hooks
Create and edit flows share a BudgetFormShell where behavior overlaps
Details, labor or time, contributions, costs or products, price, and preview are separated into focused form sections
Slug, option, and ownership helper logic lives under lib/budgets or an equivalent scoped domain location
Authored budget form files stay under 200 lines unless an exception is explicitly justified
Manual smoke covers create, edit, duplicate, delete, category selection, preview, and filtering

features.name: ops_occurrence_scheduling_refactor
features.title: Separate ops occurrence reads, generation, and scheduling UI
features.description: Make job occurrence reads and generation commands explicit, then split the occurrence dialog and scheduling helpers by responsibility.
acceptance: getJobOccurrences is read-only or the generation side effect is moved behind an explicitly named command
Occurrence generation, persistence, employees, and recurrence math have clear module ownership
JobOccurrenceDialog is split into dialog shell, form, form state, and submit helpers where useful
Scheduling-related authored files stay under 200 lines unless an exception is explicitly justified
Manual smoke covers monthly calendar load, create visit, edit visit, split occurrence, and archive flows

features.name: ops_finance_domain_refactor
features.title: Unify operational finance management and monthly rules
features.description: Create a unified Finance workspace for client payments, operational costs, and employee payments while centralizing shared summaries and assigned-month rules.
acceptance: The operations nav replaces Cobros, Costes, and Pagos with one Finanzas entry at /dashboard/financial while the three legacy routes remain functional
Finance shows one monthly recorded-only summary plus independently filtered sections for client payments, operational costs, and employee payments
Finance supports create, edit, void, payroll suggestions, employee attribution, cost categories, and BPS settings without leaving the page
Employee payments have a required assigned month, existing rows are backfilled from paymentDate, and financial screens use it without double-counting cross-month work periods
Monthly summary, payment status, and assigned-month logic live under lib/ops/finance and are reused by dashboard, costs, payroll, and Finance
Loading, empty, error, retry, responsive UI, focused calculations, lint, build when available, and authenticated browser smoke are recorded

features.name: client_boundaries_and_cleanup
features.title: Reduce client-heavy pages and clean cross-cutting debug debt
features.description: Push client components lower where practical and remove remaining debug logging, generic errors, and inconsistent cache/action wrapper patterns.
acceptance: Full-page use client boundaries in budgets and settings are reduced where server components can own the shell safely
Non-productive console.log statements are removed from budget, form-hook, dropdown, and user-data paths
Action wrappers touched by the refactor throw or return typed errors consistently with local patterns
Any intentionally client-heavy page documents the reason in the feature progress report
Verification includes init.ps1 and manual smoke for each affected route

features.name: budget_hourly_target_product_margin
features.title: Add hourly price targeting and optional product margin
features.description: Let budget authors target a total or hourly service selling price, derive the required service margin, disable product margin by default, and compare hourly prices with and without products.
acceptance: Create and edit forms expose a numeric service hourly-price target that derives the service revenue percentage
Create and edit forms expose a total service price target that derives the hourly target from total hours
Targets below the service cost per hour clamp to zero service margin
Product margin is disabled by default and products remain billed at cost when disabled
Product margin can be enabled at the existing 15 percent default and persists through create and edit
The live preview shows hourly prices both without and with products, excluding IVA
Focused calculation checks, lint, build when available, and browser smoke are recorded

features.name: budget_recent_searches
features.title: Remember recent budget searches
features.description: Persist and expose the five most recent budget search terms in the browser.
acceptance: Non-empty budget searches are saved in localStorage
At most five unique searches are kept in most-recent-first order
Recent searches appear from the budget search input and can be selected to search again
Lint and a browser smoke check pass

features.name: calendar_operational_filters
features.title: Filter the operational calendar
features.description: Let users narrow the monthly calendar and daily agenda by job, employee, visit status, and visits that need attention.
acceptance: The calendar can be filtered by job and employee using options from the loaded month
Users can additionally filter by visit status or show only visits that need attention
Job, employee, status, and attention filters compose over the same visible result set
Calendar markers, monthly metrics, and the selected-day agenda reflect the filtered visits
Active filters are summarized and can be cleared together
The empty state explains when filters hide all visits and offers a reset action
Lint and a browser smoke check pass

features.name: job_budget_option_net_price
features.title: Show budget option prices without IVA when creating jobs
features.description: Display the net price for each linked budget option in the job form instead of the stored IVA-inclusive price.
acceptance: The budget option selector displays each option price without IVA
The selected option summary uses the same net amount and labels it as excluding IVA
The change reuses shared job budget pricing rules
Focused calculation checks, lint, and a browser smoke check pass

features.name: job_excel_export
features.title: Export filtered jobs to Excel
features.description: Add a jobs-page export that downloads the jobs matching the current filters with linked price, hourly price, and relevant operational details.
acceptance: The jobs page exposes a clear Excel export button with pending and error feedback
The export contains exactly the jobs matching the current search, status, visibility, and archived filters
When archived jobs are excluded, records with archived status or an archived date are both omitted
Linked job price reuses the shared snapshot-aware IVA pricing rule and hourly price is derived from the option workload

The workbook keeps only relevant operational fields, the budget name, product inclusion and included-product price, without status, reference, budget identifiers, pricing internals, archive metadata, audit identities, or technical ids
The workbook is readable in Excel with a styled frozen header, filters, and practical column widths
Focused export checks, lint, build when available, and a browser smoke check are recorded

features.name: visits_multi_view_infinite_history
features.title: Add multi-view visits history with weekly infinite scroll
features.description: Turn the operational calendar into a Visits surface with calendar, compact list, and card views backed by weekly TanStack Query pagination.
acceptance: The dashboard navigation and calendar route present the operational surface as Visits while retaining the monthly calendar and agenda
Users can switch between Calendar, List, and Cards, with Calendar as the first default and the last selected mode persisted locally
List and Cards share a newest-first weekly infinite query that loads older matching visits without duplicate requests
Job, employee including unassigned, status, and attention filters compose consistently across all views and reset when the operational month changes
Filter options are available independently of the weeks already loaded and visit-related mutations invalidate the infinite feed safely
Initial loading, another-week loading, retryable error, empty result, and end-of-history states are explicit
Focused boundary checks, TypeScript, lint, build when available, and authenticated browser smoke are recorded
